message.content:
In Texas, tenants have a number of statutory rights designed to protect them from unfair treatment and ensure safe, habitable living conditions. Below is an overview of key tenant rights under Texas law (Texas Property Code, Chapter 24) and related statutes: | Category | Key Rights | Practical Implications | |----------|------------|------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit, two months for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | • Keep records of move‑in condition; take photos/ videos. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, and pest control.
• Must keep premises in good repair and free of health hazards. | • Report problems promptly; keep written records. | | **Repair & Deduct / Rent Withholding** | • If landlord fails to fix major repairs within 30 days after notice, tenant may withhold rent or pay and deduct from security deposit. | • Document all communication. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot enter without reasonable notice (usually 24 hrs) except emergencies. | • Keep a log of entries. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For nonpayment: 3‑day notice before eviction.
• For lease termination: 30‑day notice if lease is month‑to‑month. | • Written notices are required. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Protected classes: race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, etc. | • Landlords cannot refuse or discriminate. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease must be in writing if longer than one year.
• Must include rent amount, due date, security deposit, and other material terms. | • Review lease carefully before signing. | | **Rent Control** | • No statewide rent control; local ordinances may apply. | • Check city ordinances. | | **Eviction Process** | • Must follow court procedure; unlawful detainer suit. | • Tenants have right to contest. | | **Subletting & Assignment** | • Tenant may sublet only with landlord’s consent (unless lease prohibits). | • Obtain written permission. | | **Landlord’s Right to Enter** | • 24‑hour notice for inspections, repairs, or showing. | • Landlord must not enter during “quiet hours” (nighttime). | | **Health & Safety Codes** | • Landlord must comply with local building codes, fire safety, and sanitation regulations. | • Report violations to local authorities. | ### How to Exercise These Rights 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of lease, receipts, photographs, emails, texts, and a written log of incidents. 2. **Written Communication** – Send notices via certified mail or email with read receipt whenever possible. 3. **Know Your Local Ordinances** – Some cities (e.g., Austin, Dallas) have additional tenant protections. 4. **Seek Legal Assistance** – If you face eviction or discrimination, contact a local tenant advocacy group or attorney. 5. **File Complaints** – Report serious violations to the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA) or local housing authority. ### Resources - **Texas Property Code** – Chapter 24 (Residential Landlord‑Tenant Law) - **TDHCA** – [https://www.tdhca.state.tx.us](https://www.tdhca.state.tx.us) - **Local Tenant Advocacy Groups** – e.g., Texas Tenants Union, local legal aid clinics. --- **Disclaimer:** This summary is for informational purposes only and does not constitute legal advice. For specific situations, consult a licensed attorney familiar with Texas landlord‑tenant law.
